newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police end fruitless "horror house" dig.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police end fruitless "horror house" dig.

text.p: Police investigating a Belgian child sex ring spent several hours on Saturday excavating the site of a "horror house" where two girls' bodies were found in September, but found nothing new.
The house was destroyed overnight on Thursday in a blaze which fire services said was being treated as arson.
"We found nothing, but we had wanted to be certain," police spokesman Guy Soumoy told reporters. There were no plans to excavate the grounds further.
A separate investigation was trying to find the exact cause of the fire at the site in Jumet, a suburb of Charleroi in southern Belgium.
The house was last occupied by Frenchman Bernard Weinstein, an acquaintance of convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux who is chief suspect in Belgium's paedophile investigation.
The decomposed bodies of teenage friends An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks, missing for a year, were found on September 4 last year under a shed in the grounds of the house.
Later that month more than 3,000 local people signed a petition asking for the detached property, which they dubbed the "House of Horror", to be razed and a memorial to the victims put in its place.

Meanwhile, Soumoy said, a search at a disused mine complex in the town would continue until Sunday or Monday. Saturday's efforts had again been hampered by the cold, mud and water in the mine which had to be pumped out.
Police have gained access to 10 underground mine galleries and are looking for places where they think the paedophile gang may have hidden children and possibly bodies.
So far their search has been in vain, but four galleries have yet to be investigated.
Dutroux, who is in jail along with several alleged accomplices, has admitted abducting Marchal and Lambrecks as well as murdering Weinstein.
In August Dutroux led police to the bodies of two other girls -- Melissa Russo and Julie Lejeune -- buried alongside Weinstein in the garden of one of several houses Dutroux owned.
